title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-trailing-profit-stop review (PR #240)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #240 (backend-trailing-profit-stop), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. The review's blocking findings (a ratchet-invariant break across a same-ticker position merge, and stale frontend test fixtures/mocks breaking `yarn build`'s `tsc -b` step) went back to the parent task itself as `needs_work`, not here.

checklist.step: Vectorize `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s per-call fold: the manual Python `for` loop over `since_entry["close"]` (calling `trailing_profit_stop` and re-deriving `threshold_profit` on every iteration) is mathematically equivalent to a single vectorized pandas computation -- e.g. `profit = since_entry["close"] - entry_price`, mask by `profit >= threshold_profit`, `candidate = entry_price + fraction * (profit - threshold_profit)`, then `.where(mask).cummax()` and take the last value (or `safezone_stop` if nothing ever qualified). Cheap at today's data sizes but pays an O(N) Python-level loop plus a full `trailing_profit_stop` call per row per position per `GET /api/portfolio/risk` poll, for no behavioral benefit over the vectorized form.

Reconsider `trailing_stop`'s 'detection + exposure only' scope (documented in docs/Analyse.md and this task's own decisions): it is not wired into `evaluate_exit_flags`/the SELL-trigger logic the way `protective_stop` is, so a close below it currently has no actionable consequence anywhere in the app -- unlike protective_stop, whose own doc explicitly says a close below it is itself a SELL trigger. Worth a deliberate decision (not just an implicit non-decision) on whether/how Elder ch. 54's trailing stop should eventually gate an exit the same way, now that the field exists and is live in the API.

The `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` write-back comparison (`if position_row.trailing_stop_high_water_mark is None or trailing_stop > position_row.trailing_stop_high_water_mark: position_row.trailing_stop_high_water_mark = trailing_stop`) is inlined directly in `app.api.routers.portfolio.get_risk`'s per-position loop rather than encapsulated as a small helper in `app.portfolio.risk` alongside `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` itself. Minor 'thin router' deviation (docs/Architecture.md's 'business logic in signals/portfolio/, not embedded in route handlers' rule) -- worth moving into risk.py (e.g. an `advance_high_water_mark(position_row, candidate)`-shaped helper) for consistency with how every other risk computation in this file already lives in risk.py, not portfolio.py.

Concurrency: two overlapping `GET /api/portfolio/risk` requests for the same position each read `position_row.trailing_stop_high_water_mark` before either commits, so a lost-update race is possible (the lower of two concurrently-computed candidates could win the final `db.commit()`). Narrow window, and self-limiting in practice (the stateless recompute still floors most cases correctly), but now that this GET route mutates state at all, its write needs the same concurrency scrutiny any other mutating endpoint gets -- worth a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`-style guard or an atomic `UPDATE ... SET trailing_stop_high_water_mark = MAX(trailing_stop_high_water_mark, :candidate)` instead of read-compare-write from Python, if this is judged worth closing rather than accepting as a low-probability, self-healing race.

Non-blocking, from PR #240's round-4 re-review (code-review skill pass): the 'daily_ohlcv must already be filtered through drop_malformed_daily_bars' contract that `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`/`ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` rely on (round-3's fix) is enforced only by docstring convention, duplicated across two call sites (`get_risk`, `add_position`'s merge branch) rather than centralized inside the function itself. A third future caller of this permanent-MAX-floor function could forget to pre-filter and silently reintroduce the exact round-3 bug (a single malformed bar locking in an unrecoverable wrong high-water-mark floor) in a new code path. Worth considering having `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` filter internally (accepting the minor duplicate-filter cost when a caller already filtered) rather than trusting every future caller to remember the convention.

decisions.decision: Resolved both the 'inline write-back helper' and 'GET concurrency race' checklist items above as a byproduct of backend-trailing-profit-stop's round-2 fix (PR #240, second re-review), which moved the `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` write off `GET /api/portfolio/risk` entirely (to `POST /api/portfolio/positions`'s same-ticker-merge branch) -- not by implementing either item's literal original suggestion (an `advance_high_water_mark` helper, or a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`/atomic `UPDATE ... SET ... = MAX(...)` guard).
decisions.rationale: The helper-function item: the write-back logic now lives entirely in `app.portfolio.risk.trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` (composing `protective_stop` + `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`), with the router doing only a two-line `floor = trailing_stop_floor_before_merge(...); if floor is not None: existing.trailing_stop_high_water_mark = floor` -- the 'thin router, business logic in risk.py' goal this item wanted is satisfied by the new design, without needing the specific `advance_high_water_mark(position_row, candidate)` shape originally suggested (which was written against the now-removed GET-side write-back). The concurrency-race item: the exact race it described (two overlapping GETs racing a lost update on `db.commit()`) no longer exists, since GET never writes at all anymore. An analogous race exists at the new write site (two overlapping same-ticker merges for the same ticker), but it shares the identical read-mutate-commit transaction pattern every other field this same merge branch already mutates without any locking (`existing.quantity`, `existing.avg_cost_basis`, `existing.entry_notes`, `existing.strategy`) -- singling out `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` alone for a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`/atomic-`UPDATE` treatment would be an inconsistent special case relative to the rest of this same handler, not a response to any newly-introduced gap. Both are marked `done` here rather than leaving them open against logic that no longer exists.

decisions.decision: Vectorized `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s per-call fold: replaced the manual Python `for` loop over `since_entry["close"]` with `profit = since_entry["close"] - entry_price`, `mask = profit >= threshold_profit`, `candidate = entry_price + fraction * (profit - threshold_profit)`, then `candidate.where(mask).cummax().ffill().iloc[-1]` (falling back to `safezone_stop` when that's NaN, i.e. nothing ever qualified, or when `since_entry` is empty).
decisions.rationale: Mathematically identical output to the old per-row fold (verified against the full existing `TestRatchetTrailingProfitStop`/`TestTrailingStopFloorBeforeMerge` suites, unchanged, plus new tests added for the internal-filtering behavior below) while dropping the O(N) Python-level loop and its N calls to `trailing_profit_stop`. One subtlety the checklist item's own suggested `.where(mask).cummax()` + 'take the last value' shape didn't anticipate: pandas' `cummax()` reports NaN, not the carried-forward running max, AT the exact row position of a masked-out/NaN input (verified interactively: `pd.Series([nan,100,106.667,102.667,100.667,nan]).cummax()` ends in `NaN`, not `106.667`) -- so a naive `.cummax().iloc[-1]` silently regresses to NaN/a stale value whenever the LAST row in `since_entry` happens to be non-qualifying (e.g. a pullback on the most recent day after an earlier rally already crossed the trigger), exactly the `test_extending_history_with_more_calls_never_lowers_the_result` scenario this task's own existing test suite already covers -- caught because that test failed on first vectorization attempt. `.ffill()` after `.cummax()` closes that gap by carrying the running max forward through any trailing non-qualifying rows, so `.iloc[-1]` always reflects the true running max as of the last row; `.max()` alone (without `cummax`) would have avoided the issue too, but `.cummax().ffill()` was kept as the closer match to the checklist's own suggested approach once corrected for this edge case.

decisions.decision: Chose (a): `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` stays detection + exposure only for now -- not wired into `evaluate_exit_flags` as a new exit flag. docs/Analyse.md's existing 'Detection + exposure only ... independent of protective_stop -- a trader is meant to consider both, not treat one as superseding the other' text is reaffirmed here as a deliberate, reasoned choice (not an oversight left implicit), now backed by this explicit `decisions` entry rather than only prose in Analyse.md.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md's own 'Stop-loss placement' subsection states, specifically for `protective_stop`, that 'a close below this stop is itself a SELL trigger ... regardless of Screen 2/3 state' -- an explicit, unconditional automated-exit rule. The very next subsection (the trailing/profit-protecting stop) never restates that framing for `trailing_stop`; it only describes Elder's ch. 54 behavior (move to breakeven, then protect a growing fraction of profit) as a stop-setting TECHNIQUE, not as a second independent automatic SELL condition layered on top of the first. Wiring `trailing_stop` into `evaluate_exit_flags` as its own flag (option (b), considered and rejected here) would create two simultaneously-live, independently-computed automatic SELL triggers for the same position that can disagree in either direction (this app's own `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` schema description already states it 'can be tighter (higher) OR looser (lower) than protective_stop on any given day once triggered') -- and since `trailing_stop` is frequently ABOVE `protective_stop` post-trigger (it protects an already-locked-in profit floor), auto-flagging on it would mean the app mechanically proposes exiting many still-net-profitable positions on nothing more than an ordinary pullback below a rising floor, which cuts against Triple Screen's broader philosophy of staying with an intact trend rather than mechanically closing on every minor retracement. Rejected as a genuine near-term option: exposing `trailing_stop` alongside `protective_stop` (as this app already does) so the human trader weighs both together is the more conservative, less mechanically-aggressive choice, and matches this app's own documented framing of the two as complementary techniques rather than one superseding the other. Also considered and rejected: implementing (b) anyway, gated on an as-of-yesterday `trailing_stop` value (mirroring `protective_stop`'s own look-ahead-avoidance convention in `evaluate_exit_flags`) -- rejected because `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s signature doesn't currently expose a 'yesterday's ratchet, computed independently of today's close' value (it folds up to and including whatever `daily_ohlcv` it's handed), so this would need a signature/behavior redesign, plus new flag-naming/severity/frontend-treatment decisions the docs don't settle -- a genuine feature-scope change better made deliberately in its own dedicated task than folded into this non-blocking-followups cleanup. No code change was made for this item; docs/Analyse.md's existing wording already correctly reflects choice (a) and needed no edit.

decisions.decision: Chose to have `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` and `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` filter `daily_ohlcv` internally via `app.signals.engine.drop_malformed_daily_bars(daily_ohlcv, require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False)`, rather than continuing to rely solely on the docstring-enforced 'caller must pre-filter' convention. `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` filters as its own first step (after its existing empty/missing-column/non-positive-avg_cost_basis guards); `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` filters before slicing for its own `protective_stop` call and before its length check, and now re-checks `len(daily_ohlcv) < 2` a second time post-filter (a frame that only reached 2 raw rows by counting bars filtering then drops is exactly as uncomputable as one that never had 2 rows). `protective_stop`/`stop_from_price_action` were deliberately left unchanged (out of this checklist item's scope; they have their own separate, already-established `columns_validated`-based caller-responsibility convention).
decisions.rationale: Weighed per the checklist item's own framing: the cost of internal filtering is a redundant, idempotent no-op `dropna` call on every already-filtering caller's frame (both current callers, `get_risk` and `add_position`'s merge branch, keep their own external filter too, since that same filtered frame is also needed for other computations of theirs in the same request -- protective_stop, evaluate_exit_flags, profit_target -- not just this one call) -- cheap at today's data sizes, identical order of magnitude to the vectorized fold itself. Against that: this function is a PERMANENT MAX-floor (`persisted_high_water_mark`), so a single malformed bar reaching it unfiltered can lock in an arbitrarily wrong value no future correct computation can ever bring back down -- exactly the bug class that already recurred once (PR #240's round-3 finding, fixed by adding the caller-side filter convention in `add_position`) and was explicitly flagged as at risk of recurring a second time via a future third caller that forgets the convention (this checklist item's own wording). Moving the filter inside the function converts a docstring convention (invisible to a new caller unless they read it) into a structural guarantee no future caller can accidentally skip -- eliminating the recurring bug class outright rather than merely documenting it more clearly a second time. Verified via new regression tests: `TestRatchetTrailingProfitStop.test_filters_a_malformed_interior_bar_internally_even_when_caller_did_not`/`test_entirely_malformed_frame_falls_back_to_safezone_stop`/`test_entirely_malformed_frame_still_respects_the_persisted_floor` and `TestTrailingStopFloorBeforeMerge.test_filters_a_malformed_interior_bar_internally_even_when_caller_did_not`/`test_too_short_after_internal_filtering_returns_none` (all in `backend/tests/unit/test_portfolio_risk.py`), plus updating the existing PR #240 round-4 regression test (`test_merge_ignores_a_malformed_bar_when_capturing_the_pre_merge_floor` in `backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py`) whose own 'sanity check that this fixture reproduces the bug when left unfiltered' assumption became stale once the bug became structurally impossible regardless of caller filtering -- replaced with a defense-in-depth assertion that calling `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` directly on the raw, unfiltered frame (bypassing the router's own external filter entirely) still produces the correctly-filtered floor. Full backend suite (1244 passed) and 100% coverage on `app/portfolio/risk.py` confirmed after the change; ruff/mypy clean.

comments.summary: Vectorization correctness independently verified beyond the PR's own tests: hand-derived the edge cases the review brief called out (all-below-threshold, a series that crosses the threshold then drops back below it ending on a non-qualifying row, a single-row series above and below threshold, and a series whose very first row is at/above threshold) and additionally ran 2000 randomized comparisons of the new vectorized fold against a from-scratch reimplementation of the original per-row Python loop -- zero mismatches. The `.cummax().ffill()` fix for cummax's NaN-at-masked-row behavior is correct: cummax's skipna=True carries the true running max forward internally even though it reports NaN at the exact position of a masked-out (non-qualifying) input, and `.ffill()` correctly recovers that carried value at the final position when the last row happens to be non-qualifying. This exact scenario is (and was, pre-PR) exercised by the pre-existing `test_extending_history_with_more_calls_never_lowers_the_result` test (its final call's last close, 105, sits below the 10% breakeven trigger), which the PR's own decisions entry notes caught a first, incorrect vectorization attempt.

The internal `drop_malformed_daily_bars` filtering added to `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`/`trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` is safely idempotent when a caller has already externally filtered: `drop_malformed_daily_bars` is a `dropna(subset=...)` call, a no-op on an already-clean frame, so `get_risk`/`add_position` (both of which still filter externally, since that same filtered frame is needed for other computations in the same request) see no behavior change. `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`'s pre-filter and post-filter `len(daily_ohlcv) < 2` checks are both necessary and correctly ordered (a frame that only reaches 2 raw rows by counting bars the internal filter then drops is exactly as uncomputable as one that never had 2 rows) -- confirmed via the PR's own new `test_too_short_after_internal_filtering_returns_none`.

The 'keep trailing_stop detection-only, not wired into evaluate_exit_flags' decision is well-reasoned, not a scope-avoidance shortcut: cross-checked against docs/Analyse.md's own §7 text (line 258 in the current doc), which already states 'Detection + exposure only ... independent of protective_stop -- a trader is meant to consider both, not treat one as superseding the other' -- language this decision correctly cites and reaffirms rather than invents after the fact. The rationale's core argument (protective_stop's doc explicitly frames a close below it as an unconditional SELL trigger; trailing_stop's doc never makes that claim, and trailing_stop is frequently ABOVE protective_stop post-trigger, so auto-flagging on it would mechanically propose exiting many still-profitable positions on an ordinary pullback below a rising floor) is sound and consistent with Triple Screen's stay-with-the-trend philosophy. The considered-and-rejected alternative (a yesterday's-value-gated exit flag) is also correctly identified as needing a signature/behavior redesign this non-blocking-followups task shouldn't absorb.

Independently re-ran the full backend suite (1244 passed, 100% coverage on app/portfolio/risk.py and the whole app/ tree), ruff check app/ tests/ and mypy app/ (both clean), scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py (clean), and scripts/validate_tasks.py (296 files, clean) -- all match the PR's own claimed numbers. No API/schema change in this diff (only backend/app/portfolio/risk.py, two test files, and task-board JSON), and backend/openapi.json is confirmed untouched, consistent with the PR description. This PR touches no frontend/UI surface at all, so the browser walkthrough and persisted e2e suite steps were explicitly skipped rather than silently omitted. A parallel high-effort code-review skill pass (forked run) independently reached the same conclusion: no correctness bugs, only two minor observations (the redundant-but-idempotent double filtering, already weighed and accepted in the PR's own decisions entry, and a now-vestigial NaN-close-handling comment/branch made unreachable by the new unconditional internal filtering) -- the second is new and tracked below since it wasn't already captured anywhere durable.

Non-blocking (tracked on backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups-followups): the three new `decisions` entries this PR added all share the identical timestamp 2026-09-24T10:14:28Z, despite describing three distinct, substantial pieces of work (including one that involved a failed first vectorization attempt, a test failure, and debugging pandas' cummax-at-masked-row NaN behavior) that could not plausibly have all been recorded at the same instant. Same class of evidence-trail imprecision this project has already flagged and fixed twice on an unrelated task lineage (PR #294, PR #298).

Non-blocking (tracked on backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups-followups, from the parallel code-review skill pass): `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s vectorized-fold comment explaining that a NaN close 'naturally produces NaN profit ... excluded from the ratchet ... with no separate NaN check needed here' now describes an unreachable case in practice, since the function's own new unconditional `drop_malformed_daily_bars` call immediately above guarantees no remaining row has a NaN close. Harmless (defense-in-depth, useful if that filtering call is ever removed), not a bug.

review.notes: Full review of PR #301 (backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups), which implements the 3 remaining checklist items from the parent task's own followups (vectorize ratchet_trailing_profit_stop, decide trailing_stop's exit-flag scope, filter malformed bars internally). No blocking findings. Verified independently, not just re-reading the PR's own claims: (1) the vectorization is genuinely behavior-identical to the original loop across hand-constructed edge cases and 2000 randomized trials, and the .ffill() fix for cummax's NaN-at-masked-row quirk is correct and already covered by a pre-existing test; (2) the internal malformed-bar filtering is idempotent and doesn't change behavior for either existing caller; (3) the 'keep trailing_stop detection-only' decision faithfully reflects docs/Analyse.md's own existing wording and is soundly reasoned, not work avoidance; (4) full backend suite/coverage/ruff/mypy/validate_tasks.py/profit-target-wording-guard all independently re-run and clean, matching the PR's claims; (5) no API/schema change, so no openapi.json regeneration needed; (6) no frontend/UI surface touched, so the browser walkthrough and e2e suite steps are explicitly skipped, not silently omitted. A parallel forked code-review skill pass reached the same no-blocking-bugs conclusion. Two non-blocking findings (identical timestamps across this PR's three new decisions entries; a now-vestigial NaN-close-handling comment made unreachable by the new internal filtering) are filed on a new backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups-followups task. Accepting. Task moved to docs/tasks/done/backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups.json, state: done. Not merging -- that's pr-decision/pr-merger's job.
